name: section-helpers-requirements
body:
source: change request "section, dict and list helpers for layouts, plus .raw and .data" (untrusted prose), checked against the durable requirements and the code graph. Changes made and inconsistencies resolved:

(1) Added requirements.requirement.section-helper (child of template-language): a layout may render a named section template directly, exactly as if the instance were authored in Markdown [autonomous].
(2) Added requirements.requirement.section-helper-load-checks (child of template-build-checks): the static reference checks (existing section-usage target, literal dict keys are declared fields, required fields present/defaulted, target with min>0 child section rejected) and helper calls participate in cycle rejection [autonomous].
(3) Added requirements.requirement.dict-list-helpers (child of template-language): the dict/list constructors [autonomous].
(4) Added requirements.requirement.raw-source-context and requirements.requirement.section-data-context (children of template-context): the .raw source values and the .data section tree [autonomous].
(5) Reconciled the "v1 helper set is exactly media" law: template-language, template-context, item-context, section-template-context, domain.constraint.template-context-reserved, solution.component.renderer, solution.component.template-registry and the two agent guides now state the helper set media/section/dict/list [autonomous].
(6) requirements.constraint.reserved-template-names extended with raw and data; the reserved-name lists in template-build-checks, item-context and the agent-guide requirements updated to match [autonomous].
(7) requirements.constraint.section-cycle-error-chain and requirements.requirement.template-composition updated: a reference is a declared sections: acceptance OR a section helper call in a layout [autonomous].
(8) requirements.requirement.library-agent-guide, agent-authoring and agent-guide-drift-check updated: the guides must document the four helpers, the .raw/.data context and the raw/data reserved names, because the drift self-test derives those vocabularies from template.LayoutFuncMap / ReservedNames / ContextKeys [autonomous].
(9) Per user decision (feedback-1): requirements.requirement.section-helper-load-checks now records that a helper `body` that is a literal string in the layout is parsed at load and a heading naming a declared child section of the target is a load-time templates error, with an AC for it; requirements.requirement.section-helper now states that a non-literal body is rejected against the target's body rule at render/example time [with user].

Settled decisions (feedback-2): the four points previously drafted as open questions are confirmed by the user, and the requirement nodes were made consistent with them:
- Body-heading timing [with user]: a helper `body` heading that names a declared child section of the target is rejected when the body is validated against the target's body rule — a load-time, path-qualified templates error when the `body` argument is a literal string in the layout (section-helper-load-checks), and at render/example time when it is a non-literal expression validated against the target's body rule (section-helper).
- Non-literal fields [with user]: a `fields` argument that is not a literal `dict` call — a variable, a `.raw` / `.item.parent` pass-through, or a range value — is allowed (pass-through explicitly wanted); it loads, and its keys and required fields are checked when the target renders. section-helper-load-checks now names these pass-through forms alongside the load-time literal-dict check.
- .data and rendered list [with user]: a helper call is a direct render call, not an authored instance, so it appends neither to the caller's `.data` nor to the rendered-HTML section list; both views reflect authored instances only. section-data-context now states both explicitly (it previously named only `.data`).
- Cycle vs depth [with user]: helper calls count toward cycle rejection but not toward the six-heading-level depth bound. template-composition and section-cycle-error-chain already record the cycle side; section-depth-limit now records that a helper call is not a heading and does not extend the chain.
